lead: Venous thromboembolism is DVT and its complication, pulmonary embolism. Pregnancy raises the risk about 5 times and the puerperium more; PE is a leading direct cause of maternal death, and most fatal PEs happen after birth.
f: Pre-existing: previous VTE, thrombophilia, age over 35, BMI over 30, parity 3 or more, smoking, varicose veins, SLE, sickle cell · Obstetric: caesarean (above all in labour), pre-eclampsia, twins, prolonged labour, PPH, IUFD, IVF · Transient: immobility, surgery, hyperemesis, infection, long travel · Congenital thrombophilia: antithrombin III deficiency (highest risk), protein C or S deficiency, factor V Leiden (commonest) · Acquired: antiphospholipid syndrome · Left leg affected in about 75%: the right common iliac artery compresses the left iliac vein

DVT: leg pain and swelling, usually left; calf more than 2 cm wider; tender, warm; iliofemoral clot may give abdominal or back pain · PE: breathlessness, pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, collapse; tachycardia, tachypnoea, low SpO₂ · Massive: hypotension, raised JVP, cyanosis

sc: Both ankles swollen, painless, 36 wk → Physiological oedema
tr: One painful swollen leg in pregnancy = DVT until proven otherwise

f: Start treatment-dose LMWH first, then investigate (unless bleeding) · Baseline FBC, U&E, LFT, clotting · Compression duplex: negative but suspicion high → keep LMWH, repeat on day 4 and 7 · Iliac DVT: Doppler of the iliac vein or MRI venography · D-dimer not useful (raised in normal pregnancy) · PE: ECG commonest sinus tachycardia (S1Q3T3 suggestive only); CXR often normal; ABG low O₂ and CO₂ · Legs first: a DVT on duplex proves VTE · Normal CXR → V/Q scan; abnormal CXR → CTPA; fetal radiation risk almost nil

sc: Day 4 after CS, breathless, SpO₂ 91% → Treatment-dose LMWH before imaging

f: DVT: cellulitis, ruptured Baker's cyst, muscle strain, physiological oedema · PE: pneumonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary oedema (peripartum cardiomyopathy), aortic dissection, amniotic fluid embolism · Complications: PE, recurrence, post-thrombotic syndrome, venous gangrene · Of treatment: bleeding, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, osteoporosis

LMWH (does not cross the placenta): enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily by booking weight (50–69 kg 60 mg, 70–89 kg 80 mg twice daily) · For the rest of pregnancy and at least 6 wk after birth (3 months in total) · Stockings, leg elevation, early mobilisation · LMWH needs no routine monitoring; UFH (APTT 1.5–2.5 times) for massive PE, high bleeding risk or near delivery · Reversal: protamine (complete for UFH, partial for LMWH)

tr: Warfarin crosses the placenta: embryopathy at 6–12 wk and fetal brain bleeds later; avoid in pregnancy, safe after birth

f: Stop injections when labour or bleeding starts · No regional block within 24 h of a treatment dose (12 h after a prophylactic dose) · Restart LMWH 8–12 h after birth, at least 4 h after the epidural catheter is removed · Postpartum: LMWH or warfarin (overlap until INR 2–3 on 2 days, at least 5 days) · Both are safe in breastfeeding

sc: Last treatment dose 8 h ago, wants an epidural → No block: wait 24 h

f: Hypotension and respiratory distress · ICU, O₂, fluids · IV UFH 5000 IU then 1000–2000 IU/h · Thrombolysis or embolectomy · IVC filter if anticoagulation is contraindicated or PE recurs on it

Assess at booking, every admission, 36 wk, in labour and after birth · 0–1 risk factor: mobilise · 2 factors: LMWH 10 days postpartum · 3 factors: from 28 wk to 6 wk after birth · 4 or more: whole pregnancy + 6 wk · Previous VTE after major surgery: as 3 factors; unprovoked, oestrogen-related or with thrombophilia: whole pregnancy + 6 wk · Enoxaparin 40 mg daily (50–90 kg); 20 mg under 50 kg; 60 mg at 91–130 kg
